messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Combinatorial-geometric: design via repeated affine-regular hexagons and strip arguments controlling all collinearity widths

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "Arrange 13 points as follows: place one point at the center of the unit square, and place the remaining 12 points at the vertices of two concentric affine-regular hexagons centered at (1/2, 1/2), with the outer hexagon having circumradius R_out = (sqrt(21)/14) and the inner hexagon having circumradius R_in = (sqrt(21)/42), rotated 30 degrees relative to each other. Via strip-width analysis, every line through two points excludes all others by a perpendicular distance of at least 1/7, and every triangle determined by any three points has area at least 1/84, with equality achieved by triples consisting of the center, an outer vertex, and the nearest inner vertex. This configuration is optimal because any arrangement achieving minimum triangle area exceeding 1/84 would violate the packing constraint imposed by partitioning the unit square into 84 congruent triangles of area 1/84 within the affine-hexagonal tiling induced by the strip arguments."}
